description: Mostly early-game: a bottom-row configuration where the opponent has stones at the bottom of columns 1 and 5 (often 4 too) and I have the bottom of columns 3 and 6, with no opponent stone at the bottom of 3 or 6. Opponent stones directly above theirs in row 2 (columns 1,4,5,6) suppress it; my stone on (row 2, col 3) boosts it. Firing fades as the board fills; late-game firing is only partly explained.
effect: None measurable: forcing it high or off changes move probabilities by at most about 0.09 (4 positions tested).
notes: Best dev F1 0.243 (P 0.28, R 0.21), AUROC 0.60 (graded variant 0.705), sim share 0.07. Minimal pairs confirm the bottom-row core (them{1,4,5}+me{3,6} = 5.5 at ply 5; dropping col1 or col5 stones halves it; mirror image ~0.3) but per-cell effects are context dependent and late-game firing depends on assorted upper stacks (e.g. their stone at (2,6)). Behaves like a diffuse positional mixture; may be a random direction. 5 of 8 score calls used.
